sources.instruction: Read the programme list or official feed through the three-day Beijing window; distinguish interviews from recaps and articles.
Check video and written interview lists; articles alone are not interviews.
Check written interviews and the official podcast; chapter headings alone do not establish interview facts.
Use official RSS timestamps and readable episode notes; convert timestamps to Beijing before excluding a previous-local-day episode.
Check miner earnings transcripts and issuer webcast pages; record the source timezone and distinguish the call from the results release.
Read data/conference_calendar.json; check hosts, speakers and replays for active events. Record not_applicable only when no event overlaps the window.
Use ?pg=2, ?pg=3, etc. until the Beijing window is covered. Save every in-window listing, including candidates later excluded for metal or relevance; record EST/EDT explicitly.

Locate the official daily announcement list or an equivalent complete dated index; paginate through the window. Read issuer/ASX PDFs, not only a search-results subset. Save the actual list URL and boundary evidence.
Use the existing Mining collector or an equivalent actual browser category read; retain the list and date boundary. Search-engine results cannot replace category discovery.
Read the category through the Beijing window, retaining boundary evidence; verify article publication timestamps separately.
Read the category through the Beijing window, retaining boundary evidence; verify article publication timestamps separately.

Check dated copper social-inventory updates and readable Chinese/English originals. Keep social inventories, warehouse warrants and exchange inventories separate. A failed body decode is pending verification, not an editorial rejection.
Check metals/mining releases; a marketing shell, empty feed or stale feed is degraded discovery, not a healthy zero. Use issuer releases as body fallbacks.
Locate the current mining release list and preserve failures of retired industry URLs.
Check dated mining issuer releases, including drilling and project funding, through the window.
Read the industry list; for body timeouts try issuer IR and clearly attributed release syndication.
Locate the current metals/mining newsroom, paginate through the window and record the actual URL.
Page back to the Beijing-window cutoff; the latest UK evening page alone does not complete the source.
Check SENS and dated mining announcements; report incomplete official-tape access honestly.
Check relevant issuer IR, government/regulatory sources, equipment orders and official exchange inventory releases; preserve search scope and limitations.
